name: Random Forest
learningObjectives: Understand how ensemble methods combine multiple weak learners
Learn about bootstrap sampling and its role in reducing overfitting
Explore random feature selection and its impact on model diversity
Interpret out-of-bag (OOB) error as a validation metric
Recognize the bias-variance tradeoff in ensemble methods

controls.label: Dataset
controls.tooltip: Choose a classification dataset to train on

controls.label: Number of Trees
controls.tooltip: Number of decision trees in the forest. More trees generally improve performance but increase computation time.

controls.label: Max Tree Depth
controls.tooltip: Maximum depth of each decision tree. Deeper trees can capture more complex patterns but may overfit.

controls.label: Min Samples to Split
controls.tooltip: Minimum number of samples required to split an internal node. Higher values prevent overfitting.

controls.label: Min Samples per Leaf
controls.tooltip: Minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node. Higher values create smoother models.

controls.label: Bootstrap Sampling
controls.tooltip: Whether to use bootstrap sampling when building trees. Enables out-of-bag error estimation.

visualizations.title: Classification Data & Decision Boundary
visualizations.description: Scatter plot showing the classes and the ensemble decision boundary

visualizations.title: Decision Boundary (Ensemble Predictions)
visualizations.description: Heatmap showing the combined predictions from all trees in the forest

visualizations.title: Out-of-Bag Score
visualizations.description: OOB score progression as more trees are added to the forest

visualizations.title: Confusion Matrix
visualizations.description: Matrix showing classification performance across all classes
